subject: Cooking
title: Stress Eating: Cortisol's Appetite
description: A fast breakdown of Stress Eating: Cortisol's Appetite for builders.

hook.text: Under deadline pressure, you reach for chips, not carrots. Cortisol is making that choice for you.

buildup.text: Chronic stress elevates cortisol, a hormone that increases appetite — especially for high-calorie foods.

discovery.text: Cortisol redirects the brain's focus toward calorie-dense foods that provide quick energy for 'survival.'

twist.text: This system evolved for physical threats like predators. Modern stress is mental — but the body can't tell.

climax.text: High-fat comfort food actually lowers cortisol temporarily, reinforcing the stress-eating loop.

punchline.text: Stress eating isn't weakness. It's a survival reflex misfiring.

quiz.question: What hormone drives increased appetite during chronic stress?

details.summary: Chronic stress elevates cortisol, which specifically increases appetite for high-calorie comfort foods. This is not a failure of willpower — it is a hormonal response evolved to replenish energy stores after physical threats.
details.whyItMatters: Framing stress eating as hormonal rather than moral failure reduces shame and opens the door to effective interventions targeting cortisol management rather than willpower.
takeaways: Cortisol specifically drives appetite for high-fat, high-sugar foods
The response evolved for physical threats, not psychological stress
Exercise reduces cortisol more effectively than food does long-term

faq.question: Why does stress specifically target high-calorie food cravings?
faq.answer: Cortisol evolved to prepare the body for sustained physical effort after threats. High-calorie foods rapid replenish energy stores. The system cannot distinguish between running from a predator and a work deadline, so it triggers the same energy-seeking response for psychological stress.

faq.question: What actually reduces cortisol-driven eating?
faq.answer: Exercise is the most effective cortisol reducer because it completes the physical stress cycle the hormone was designed for. Sleep, social connection, and even 10 minutes of deep breathing measurably lower cortisol. Addressing the stress itself is more effective than willpower against the craving.
